title: Panorra API Go New Project Report

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 21/08/26

✅ Implementation: Recommendation Score Update Cron

Route

GET /cronjob/update-recommendation-scores

Unauthenticated — covered by the existing /cronjob/* entry in cmd/main.go's IgnoreAuthPath; no auth-path change was needed.

Changes

  • Added migrations/20260821_recommendation_scores.sql:
    • ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS score_velocity_24h/_7d/_30d, score_quality (all FLOAT8 NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) and scored_at TIMESTAMPTZ (nullable — NULL means "never scored", which is what puts a post first in the candidate ordering).
    • CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS post_engagement_snapshots (id, post_id uuid, captured_at, counters jsonb) with two indexes: (post_id, captured_at) for the per-post history read, and (captured_at) for the retention prune.
    • CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS interest_category_map (interest_key, category_id), seeded with a draft mapping from the interest keys and categories observed in the dev DB (2026-08-21) — flagged in the PRD (§12.1) as needing product confirmation before it ships beyond dev. This table is written by nothing in this repo; it is read by panorra-api-go's recommendations/* endpoints.
  • Added Models/PostEngagementSnapshot.go — id, post_id uuid, captured_at, counters json.RawMessage (type:jsonb).
  • Added Utils/Recommendation/Scoring.go — pure functions, no DB or HTTP: EnvFloat/EnvInt (env-tunable knobs; EnvInt rejects zero and negative values so a bad RECO_CRON_BATCH can never reach Limit() and cancel the batch cap), WeightsFromEnv (per-action engagement weights), CountersToFloats (ES doc → known counter fields), WeightedEngagement, VelocityScore (never negative, guards zero-duration windows), QualityScore, and WindowScores (buckets a sorted snapshot list into 24h/7d/30d velocities). Covered by Scoring_test.go.
  • Added Action/V1/Cronjob/UpdateRecommendationScores.go — the cron handler (flow below).
  • Added UpdateRecommendationScores to Controllers/V1/CronjobController.go and registered GET /cronjob/update-recommendation-scores in Routes/V1/CronjobRoutes.go, alongside the existing update-score-timeline entry.
  • Added cmd/migrate/ — the runner that applies migrations/*.sql. See Migration below.

Flow

  1. Read RECO_CRON_BATCH (default 50) and the per-action engagement weights from env (RECO_SCORE_VIEW/_LIKE/_COMMENT/_SHARE/_BOOKMARK).
  2. Query the batch of candidate posts: is_publish = true, banned = false, visibility = 'public', ordered by posts.scored_at ASC NULLS FIRST — never-scored posts first, then the stalest ones. Capped at the batch size. Ordering reads a plain column rather than aggregating post_engagement_snapshots, so the candidate query never scans the snapshot table.
  3. For each candidate post:
    1. Compute the static quality score from the post's own metadata: +0.4 if it has a panorama, +0.2 if it has a thumbnail, +0.2/+0.1 for description length (≥30 vs >0 runes, not bytes), +0.2 if it has a location name. This is done before the Elasticsearch call, because it derives only from columns already selected and therefore stays valid even when ES is unreachable.
    2. Fetch the post's current engagement document from Elasticsearch (post_<prefix> index, post_<slug> doc) via ElasticSearch.RetrieveElastic.
    3. If the ES fetch fails (ES down, or the post has no document yet): run a quality-only UPDATE posts SET score_quality, scored_at, increment skipped, and move to the next candidate. score_velocity_* is deliberately left at its previous value, and no snapshot row is written. Both alternatives are worse: writing zero velocities would drop a genuinely trending post out of every ranking for a cycle, and snapshotting zero counters would become a later window's baseline and manufacture a phantom spike (a post at 5200 weighted engagement would read as (5200 − 0) / 24h instead of its real rate). Advancing scored_at is still correct here — without it, a post whose ES document is permanently missing would stay the stalest candidate forever and starve the rest of the batch.
    4. On success: convert the raw counter document into a weighted "current engagement" number.
    5. Load that post's snapshot history from the last 30 days, oldest first.
    6. For each of the three windows (24h, 7d, 30d), find the oldest snapshot still inside that window and compute (current weighted − that snapshot's weighted) / hours elapsed → the velocity for that window. A window with no snapshot inside it stays 0.
    7. Insert one new row into post_engagement_snapshots with the just-fetched counters — this becomes the baseline the next run diffs against. A failed insert is logged and treated as non-fatal: the scores below were still computed from real counters, so they are worth persisting.
    8. UPDATE posts SET score_velocity_24h/_7d/_30d, score_quality, scored_at for this post, then increment processed. A failed update is logged and the loop continues — one bad post never aborts the batch.
  4. After the batch, delete all post_engagement_snapshots rows older than 31 days (30-day max window + 1 day slack).
  5. Return {"valid": true, "processed": N, "skipped": M} with an explicit c.Status(fiber.StatusOK). processed counts posts fully scored (velocity + quality); skipped counts posts where ES was unavailable and only quality was refreshed. The explicit status is required, not decorative: RetrieveElastic writes a 500 directly onto this shared fiber.Ctx when a document lookup misses, and c.JSON alone does not reset a status code set earlier on the same context.

Because the candidate query always prioritizes the least-recently-scored posts, running this on a fixed interval eventually cycles through the entire published post set, refreshing each post's velocity roughly once per (total published posts / batch size) runs — it does not recompute every post on every run.

Sizing caveat: for score_velocity_24h to be non-zero for a post, that post needs two snapshots inside a 24-hour span, which requires roughly runs_per_day × RECO_CRON_BATCH ≥ 2 × published_posts. RECO_CRON_BATCH and the scheduler interval must be sized against the real published-post count, or the 24h window will read 0 for most of the catalogue.

Tests

Scoring_test.go covers, as pure-function unit tests with no DB/HTTP fixtures:

  • EnvInt: rejects -1 and 0 in favour of the default, accepts a valid positive value.
  • WeightedEngagement arithmetic against a hand-computed value.
  • CountersToFloats parsing from the map[string]interface{} shape Elasticsearch/encoding/json produce, including missing/junk keys.
  • VelocityScore: positive delta, the "never negative" clamp on a negative delta, and the zero-duration-window guard.
  • QualityScore: full, empty, and partial-credit inputs.
  • WindowScores: a 3-point fixture at known ages, asserting the 24h/7d/30d deltas match hand-computed values, plus a no-snapshots case (all zero).

cmd/migrate/main_test.go covers migration-filename parsing (VERSION_name.sql, malformed name, empty body) and SQL statement splitting.

The cron handler itself (the DB/ES-calling code in UpdateRecommendationScores.go) is not unit-tested, matching this repo's existing cron-handler convention — UpdateScoreTimeline.go is likewise untested; both are exercised via manual smoke test instead.

Migration

The target database is CockroachDB (Postgres wire protocol, port 26257), which is why 20260821_recommendation_scores.sql uses CRDB-only syntax (STRING, inline INDEX inside CREATE TABLE, now():::TIMESTAMPTZ) matching the existing files in migrations/.

cmd/migrate globs migrations/*.sql (top level only), sorts by the VERSION_ filename prefix, and applies each unapplied file, recording it in a public.schema_migrations ledger so reruns are no-ops. DSNs come from the environment so no internal host or credential is committed:

MIGRATE_DSN_DEV='postgresql://…@…:26257/panorra_dev?sslmode=disable' go run ./cmd/migrate -target=dev up
go run ./cmd/migrate -target=local up   # loopback default, no env needed

The migration is also safe to apply directly — it is idempotent on its own (IF NOT EXISTS throughout, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the seed):

psql "postgresql://…@…:26257/panorra_dev?sslmode=disable" -f migrations/20260821_recommendation_scores.sql

20260821_recommendation_scores.sql is the only migration this feature needs.

Verification

gofmt -l src/ cmd/
go build ./...
go vet ./src/... ./cmd/...
go test ./...

Results: build, vet, and gofmt clean; full test suite passes (7 Scoring_test.go cases and 2 cmd/migrate cases pass; no existing test regressed).

Not yet done, deferred at user's request:

  • The migration has not been applied to any database — the user runs it manually.
  • No external scheduler has been configured to hit GET /cronjob/update-recommendation-scores. This repo has no in-code scheduler for any cron endpoint (including the existing update-score-timeline) — triggering is infra-managed, outside this codebase. PRD §12.4 proposes a 15-minute interval, matching the existing cron infrastructure's cadence, but this is not yet confirmed or wired up.
  • No manual smoke test has been run against a live server/database.

Review history

Three rounds of PR review shaped the current handler; the fixes are recorded here because the reasoning is not obvious from the final code:

  1. Starvation loop. Candidates were originally ordered by an aggregate over post_engagement_snapshots. A post whose ES fetch failed wrote no snapshot, so its ordering key stayed NULL and it was re-picked on every run forever. Fixed by adding the dedicated posts.scored_at column and ordering on it, which also removed the full snapshot-table scan from the candidate query.
  2. Poisoned baselines. An interim fix let the loop fall through with zero counters, which persisted zero-counter snapshots that later became velocity baselines. Fixed by gating the snapshot insert on a successful ES fetch. EnvInt was added in the same round after RECO_CRON_BATCH=-1 was found to reach Limit(-1), which cancels the limit and scores every post in a single request.
  3. Zeroed velocities. Round 2 left the score UPDATE unconditional, so an ES failure persisted v24 = v7 = v30 = 0. Fixed by computing quality before the ES call and splitting the failure path into the quality-only update described in the Flow section — stale velocity beats wrong velocity.

Background

The existing score cron (UpdateScoreTimeline, GET /cronjob/update-score-timeline) is reactive: it drains a score_update_containers queue and recomputes posts.score_mostpopular/score_timeline per triggered post/user action. It has no concept of a time window — it is an all-time-vs-relative score, not "how much engagement in the last 24h/7d/30d".

The personalized-explore epic (#506, PRD in panorra-api-go's docs/prd/2026-08-21-personalized-explore-prd.md) needs windowed engagement velocity to power new recommendations/* endpoints (built in panorra-api-go, which shares this repo's Postgres/CockroachDB instance). Those endpoints need a trending-style signal ("gaining engagement fast right now") that the existing all-time score cannot express.

Decision: keep the new scoring cron in this repo (panorra-api-go-new), alongside the existing score-cron infrastructure it extends, rather than in panorra-api-go where the PRD originally proposed it. The endpoints that read the resulting scores stay in panorra-api-go.

Objective

Add a new, unauthenticated, poll-style cron endpoint that periodically snapshots each candidate post's Elasticsearch engagement counters and recomputes:

  • posts.score_velocity_24h / _7d / _30d — weighted engagement gained per hour, per window.
  • posts.score_quality — a static quality score from post metadata.

so panorra-api-go's recommendation endpoints can rank by recent momentum instead of only all-time popularity.

Scope

  • Migration: 4 new posts columns (score_velocity_24h/_7d/_30d, score_quality), new post_engagement_snapshots table (per-run counter snapshots), new interest_category_map table (KYC interest key → category ID, seeded with a draft mapping).
  • Utils/Recommendation scoring-math package: pure functions only (weighting, velocity, quality, interest parsing, window bucketing), unit tested, no DB/HTTP dependency.
  • Models.PostEngagementSnapshot GORM model.
  • Cron action UpdateRecommendationScores + controller wrapper + route GET /cronjob/update-recommendation-scores, registered in the existing Cronjob route group.
  • Auth exemption: none needed — the existing /cronjob/* wildcard in cmd/main.go's IgnoreAuthPath already covers it.

Constraints

  • No new Go module dependency.
  • Batch bounded per run (env RECO_CRON_BATCH, default 200) — must never scan the entire posts table in one run.
  • Reuse this repo's own idioms, not panorra-api-go's (they diverged):
    • ElasticSearch.RetrieveElastic (returns []postgres.Jsonb, error), not V1RetrieveElastic.
    • os.Getenv("PREFIX"), not Config.Prefix (this repo's Config package has no Prefix).
    • json.RawMessage with a type:jsonb gorm tag for jsonb columns (matches Models/UserActivityLog.go), not postgres.Jsonb.
    • ?::jsonb cast on raw Exec params (matches existing jsonb-write call sites), not an untyped placeholder.
  • Snapshot retention capped at 31 days (30-day max window + 1 day slack); pruned every run.
  • Must not touch score_mostpopular, score_timeline, or score_update_containers — this is a parallel, independent scoring system, not a replacement.

Acceptance Criteria

  • go build ./... and go test ./... pass.
  • GET /cronjob/update-recommendation-scores returns {"valid":true,"processed":N}.
  • On a post's first-ever run: velocity stays 0 (no prior snapshot to diff against). A later run, after new engagement and with a prior snapshot present, produces a non-zero velocity for the covering window(s).
  • post_engagement_snapshots rows older than 31 days are deleted every run.
  • Scoring math is unit-tested in isolation (no DB/HTTP fixtures), matching this repo's pure-function test convention.
  • Scheduling (how often this endpoint gets hit) is out of scope for this task — see the implementation doc's Verification section for what remains open.
